messages.subject: Creation of Coverage
parts:
Ok I'm new to this forum.  I've tried searching for my issue and found related questions, but none of the threads seem to help.

Very simple. I've only ever used Distance to analyze existing survey data.  Now I'm trying to create a survey design.  I have a shapefile with a single polygon that I have added a LinkID field to.  The projection is Projected Coordinate System: NAD_1983_UTM_Zone_11N, Transverse_Mercator,False_Easting 500000.00000000 False_Northing: 0.00000000 Central_Meridian:-117.00000000 Scale_Factor:0.99960000 Latitude_Of_Origin: 0.00000000 Linear Unit: Meter  

I matched the default projection for the project to the above (see below)

It is a large survey area 662051 acres.  It displays ok in the Map View, when I move my cursor, the coordinates are correct.  The map tips does not seem to work for it though so perhaps something is wrong.

When I go to create a coverage, no matter what distance I select, I get the initial message telling me that it will generate X number of points and may take a long time and then every time (even if I try a grid spacing of 100m which is ridiculous) I get the error

"No grid points fell inside the survey area.  You should probably try a smaller grid spacing next time"

Nothing gets created

I have created a new project, re-exported the shapefile from the original, double checked that my parameters are ok even tried to use a different projection, but I cannot get this to work.  I am sure it is something very simple, but I'll be darned if I can figure it out.  

Here are the Project Geographic Properties:
Geographic Coordinate System "North American 1983"
Projection of Shapefile Data "Transverse Mercator" Parameters: False Easting 500000, False Northing 0, Central Meridian -117, Scale Factor 0.9996 Latitude of Origin 0 
Shapefile Units  "Meter"

Maps and Geographic Calculations:
Geographic Coordinate System "North American 1983"
Projection of Shapefile Data "Transverse Mercator" Parameters: False Easting 500000, False Northing 0, Central Meridian -117, Scale Factor 0.9996 Latitude of Origin 0 
Map Units  "Meter"

Someone enlighten me please I feel really foolish that I cannot accomplish this simple task.  Even if its just a link to another thread, I would really appreciate it.

Thanks
Marguerite

Hi Margueritre

I had several issues also trying to import defined areas from shapefiles created outside DISTANCE.

I´ve found a workaround. At the end  copy and paste the vertex of the study area created oustide Distance into the study area.

The steps I use (maybe there are other shortcuts) are:

Create your study area in a GIS
Ita has  to be projected, no matter which projection as at the end you will work with meters or km. 
Once you have the Polygons, create from the polygons a feature of points which are in turn the vertex of the Polygon/s
On this point features create columns wich in turn are filled with x and y locations of each vertex
Export them as text file, open and copy them to clipboard.

(Take care of shapes like islands or lakes, they need separators that defines closed areas or "hollows")

Then go to Distance 
Create a Study Area without a Coordinate System.
The go to the Data Tab, select the Study Area, at the right you see the Contents of the Layer, double click on the word "Polygon" and a window opens offering to you to possibility to paste all the vertexs from the clipboard.

And then voilá. You have your survey area created, and you may map and create a coverage.

Take care that the last lone in the vertes text file is not without data, because otherwise for some reason your map of the survey area will show very small, as if DISTANCE was doing a far away zoom

If this happens go again, double click the Polygon and will see at the bottom an "separator" that needs to be deleted


This is purely empirical, but  hope this helps.
